page: Amazon Web Services c8i.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. It features 384 vCPUs across 192 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic operations. The processor's L3 cache of 480 MB and advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, contribute to top-decile scores in Passmark CPU tests and multi-threaded decompression. In database operations and Redis SET benchmarks, the server registers top-tier throughput. However, while prompt processing for large language models ranks in the top 25%, text generation speeds fall to average or poor tiers due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture delivers high compute density and direct hardware access, eliminating hypervisor overhead for demanding workloads. The primary tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, which limits its efficiency for real-time LLM text generation or massive local data caching. This hardware profile is optimized for high-throughput parallel processing, scientific simulations, heavy database operations, and multi-threaded compilation tasks.
